input.source_text: class A { public async fun m(g) -> Symbol { let v = await g; :old } } let a = A.new(); let g = Gate.new(); let entered_task = a.m(g); let replaced = A.open() { |t| t.define_method(:m) { |arg| :new } }; let posted = Gate.complete(g, 1); let entered = Host.run(entered_task); let later = A.new().m(g); [entered, later]

applicability.reason: Supported. C160 keeps a frame that has ENTERED on the body it selected while a LATER send selects the replacement. The row was held because its schedule is prose - enter, pause, commit, resume - with no runnable source. An async suspension expresses exactly that pause: the frame is entered, parked on a Gate, a replacement commits while it is parked, and `Host.run` resumes it. The resumed frame answers :old and the later send answers :new, which is the whole of what the schedule asked for.
